# Thrust-Type Food Cutting Apparatus

## Overview

The apparatus disclosed herein is a thrust-type food cutting device designed to safely and efficiently process food products through a manually operated cutting mechanism. The core components of this device include a blade set, a food product pusher, and a manually operated pusher arm, which work in concert to facilitate controlled cutting motion while prioritizing user safety.

## Self-Stable Resting-Open Position

A key safety feature of the pusher arm is its self-stable resting-open position. In this configuration, the pusher arm naturally maintains the food product pusher at a distance from the blade set when not actively engaged by the user. This design ensures that during the loading phase, when the user is placing food product into the device, there is no risk of accidental contact between the food product pusher and the blade set. The self-stable nature of this open position means that the mechanism requires no additional locking or holding force from the user to remain safely retracted—it inherently returns to and maintains this safe configuration through its own mechanical design.

## Chassis and Pivoting Link Embodiment

In one particular embodiment of the invention, the apparatus incorporates a chassis that serves as the structural foundation for the mechanism, along with a pivoting link that connects the pusher arm to this chassis. This pivoting link creates what is referred to as a movable fulcrum pivot—a pivot point that is not fixed in position but rather shifts as the mechanism operates. This movable fulcrum is instrumental in achieving the self-stable resting-open position, as it allows the geometry of the pusher arm assembly to naturally settle into the safe, open configuration through the interplay of mechanical forces and the pivot's changing position throughout the range of motion.

## Retractable Food Product Stabilizer

To further enhance the functionality and safety of the cutting apparatus, an additional embodiment may incorporate a retractable food product stabilizer. This component serves the important function of holding the loaded food product securely in place during the initial stages of the cutting operation, preventing unwanted shifting or movement of the item as the user begins to apply force to the pusher arm. As the food product pusher advances toward the blade set during the cutting stroke, this stabilizer automatically retracts out of the way, ensuring it does not interfere with the cutting action or the passage of the blade set through the food product.

## Integrated Combined Functionality

Notably, the retractable food product stabilizer is not necessarily a standalone feature but can be integrated directly with the self-stabilizing pusher arm mechanism described above. This integration allows both safety and functional features—the self-stable resting-open position and the automatic retraction of the food stabilizer—to operate through a unified mechanical system. By combining these functionalities, the apparatus achieves a more streamlined design, potentially reducing the number of separate components required while ensuring that both the loading safety feature and the food stabilization feature work in coordinated harmony throughout the cutting cycle.

# Thrust-Type Food Cutting Apparatus

## Background and Overview

Food cutting apparatuses designed for slicing, dicing, or otherwise portioning food products—such as fruits, vegetables, and similar items—must balance several competing demands: user safety, operational efficiency, ease of loading, and precision of the cut itself. Traditional thrust-type cutting devices, in which a food product is pushed through a stationary blade set by manual force, have historically struggled to adequately secure food products during the loading phase. This can result in misaligned cuts, inconsistent portion sizes, or unsafe conditions where fingers may come into proximity with the blade set during loading or operation.

The present apparatus addresses these longstanding issues through an integrated mechanical design that combines a blade set, a food product pusher, a manually operated pusher arm, and a novel retractable food product stabilizer, all working in coordinated fashion through a pivoting linkage system connected to the apparatus chassis.

## Structural Components

### Blade Set
At the core of the apparatus is a blade set, fixed within the chassis, configured to perform the actual cutting or slicing operation as the food product is driven through it. The blade set may be configured in various patterns depending on the desired cut—whether straight slices, cross-cut dicing, or wedge-style portioning—but in all cases remains stationary during operation, relying on the motion of the food product itself to effect the cut.

### Food Product Pusher
The food product pusher is the component that makes direct contact with the food item, applying force to drive it through the blade set. This pusher is mechanically linked to the manually operated pusher arm, translating the user's manual force into linear motion directed at the blade set.

### Pusher Arm and Pivoting Link
The manually operated pusher arm serves as the primary user interface for operating the device. Rather than being rigidly fixed to the chassis, the pusher arm is connected via a pivoting link, allowing it to rotate about a fixed point relative to the chassis. This pivoting connection is central to the apparatus's functionality, as it allows the arm—and by extension, the food product pusher—to move through an arc from a raised, open loading position down through to a fully advanced, cutting position.

### Retractable Food Product Stabilizer
Perhaps the most innovative element of the design is the retractable food product stabilizer. This component is positioned to engage and secure the food product during the loading phase, holding it firmly in place and in proper alignment with the blade set before the cutting stroke begins. Unlike static stabilizing features found in earlier designs, this stabilizer is designed to retract automatically as the cutting stroke progresses, moving out of the path of the pusher and blade set as the pusher arm advances.

## Operational Characteristics

### Self-Stable Resting-Open Position

One of the key advantages of this design is that the pivoting link and associated components are configured such that the apparatus naturally settles into a self-stable resting-open position when not in active use. In this position, the pusher arm remains elevated and the stabilizer is deployed and available, creating an open, accessible space for the user to load the food product. Because this position is self-stable—meaning it is maintained without requiring the user to hold or brace the mechanism—the loading process becomes significantly safer and more convenient. The user's hands are free to properly position the food product against the stabilizer without simultaneously having to manage the weight or position of the pusher arm.

### Automatic Stabilizer Retraction

As the user begins the cutting stroke by pressing down on the pusher arm, the mechanical linkage causes the food product pusher to advance toward the blade set. Simultaneously, this same motion triggers the retractable stabilizer to withdraw from its engaged position. This automatic retraction is synchronized with the advancing pusher, ensuring that the stabilizer does not obstruct the cutting stroke or interfere with the blade set, while still providing maximum support to the food product for as long as possible during the initial phase of the cut.

This synchronization between pusher advancement and stabilizer retraction serves two critical purposes. First, it maintains food product alignment and stability for the longest practical duration, which directly translates to more precise and consistent cuts. Second, it ensures that the stabilizer mechanism itself never becomes an obstacle or safety hazard during the cutting motion, as it is fully retracted by the time the pusher reaches the blade set.

## Advantages of the Design

The combination of these features—the blade set, food product pusher, pivoting pusher arm, and retractable stabilizer—results in an apparatus that meaningfully improves upon prior thrust-type cutting devices in several respects:

1. **Enhanced Safety**: The self-stable open position and automatic stabilizer engagement reduce the risk of accidental injury during loading, as the user's hands remain clear of the blade set until the food product is properly secured.

2. **Improved Usability**: The self-stable resting position eliminates the need for the user to manually hold the pusher arm open during loading, streamlining the overall operation and making the device more accessible to users of varying strength and dexterity.

3. **Greater Cutting Precision**: By securing the food product during loading and maintaining that stability until the cutting stroke is well underway, the apparatus ensures more consistent, accurate cuts with reduced product waste or misalignment.

4. **Mechanical Simplicity**: Despite the sophistication of its coordinated motion, the apparatus achieves these benefits through a relatively simple mechanical linkage system, reducing the potential for mechanical failure and simplifying manufacture and maintenance.

## Conclusion

This thrust-type food cutting apparatus represents a thoughtful integration of safety, usability, and precision through its combination of a blade set, food product pusher, pivoting pusher arm, and retractable stabilizer mechanism. By achieving a self-stable resting-open position for loading and automatically retracting the stabilizer in coordination with the cutting stroke, the design addresses core challenges that have historically affected similar devices, offering an improved solution for safe and effective food product cutting.

# Über das Wort "Such"

Das kleine Wort "such" führt im Deutschen ein bescheidenes, aber vielseitiges Dasein. Es taucht in unterschiedlichen Zusammenhängen auf und zeigt dabei erstaunliche Flexibilität.

**Als Imperativ**

Am häufigsten begegnet uns "such" als Befehlsform des Verbs "suchen". Ob wir einem Hund zurufen "Such!", um ihn auf die Fährte eines Balles zu schicken, oder jemandem sagen "Such dir etwas Schönes aus" – die Aufforderung zur aktiven Suche steckt im Kern dieses Wortes.

**Als Wortbestandteil**

In zusammengesetzten Wörtern entfaltet "such" seine volle Kraft: Die *Suchmaschine* ist aus unserem digitalen Alltag nicht mehr wegzudenken, die *Ursache* verweist auf das, was am Anfang einer Kette steht, und die *Untersuchung* beschreibt den systematischen Prozess des genaueren Hinschauens.

**Ein Symbol des Menschseins**

Vielleicht ist das eigentlich Interessante an diesem Wort, dass es eine grundlegende menschliche Haltung beschreibt: das Suchen selbst. Menschen suchen nach Antworten, nach Sinn, nach verlorenen Gegenständen, nach Lösungen für Probleme. Diese Suche treibt Wissenschaft, Kunst und persönliche Entwicklung an.

In gewisser Weise ist das ganze Leben eine fortwährende Suche – nach Glück, nach Erkenntnis, nach dem richtigen Weg. Das kleine Wort "such" trägt somit eine tiefere Bedeutung in sich, als seine Kürze zunächst vermuten lässt: Es steht sinnbildlich für die menschliche Neugier und den unstillbaren Drang, die Welt zu verstehen und in ihr etwas zu finden.

Ob beim Verlegen der Schlüssel oder bei den großen Fragen des Lebens – das Suchen bleibt eine Konstante menschlicher Existenz, verdichtet in einem unscheinbaren, viersilbigen Wort.

# PATENT APPLICATION

## TITLE OF INVENTION
Manual Food Chopper with Self-Retaining Open Position Pusher Arm and Retractable Food Stabilizer

---

## ABSTRACT

A manual food chopping apparatus is disclosed comprising a housing defining a chopping chamber, a blade assembly disposed within the chamber, a pusher arm pivotally mounted to the housing, and a retractable food stabilizer. The pusher arm includes a detent mechanism configured to releasably retain the arm in a fully open position, thereby allowing hands-free loading of food items into the chopping chamber without requiring the user to manually hold the arm open. Upon application of downward force by a user, the detent mechanism disengages, permitting the pusher arm to travel through its chopping stroke and actuate the blade assembly. The retractable food stabilizer, positioned adjacent to or integrated within the chopping chamber, is movable between an extended position, in which it contacts and secures food items against lateral movement during the chopping operation, and a retracted position, in which it is withdrawn to allow for unobstructed loading, chopping of larger items, or cleaning of the device. The stabilizer may be biased toward one position by a spring element and manually or automatically transitioned between positions via a slide, button, or lever mechanism. The combination of the self-retaining pusher arm and retractable stabilizer improves ease of use, reduces the number of hands required for operation, enhances chopping consistency and safety, and simplifies maintenance of the device.

---

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

### Field of the Invention

The present invention relates generally to manual kitchen food preparation devices, and more particularly to a manual food chopper incorporating a pusher arm with a self-retaining open configuration and a retractable stabilizing mechanism for securing food during the chopping process.

### Background

Conventional manual food choppers typically require a user to hold the pusher arm in an open position with one hand while loading food items into the chopping chamber with the other hand. This two-handed requirement can be cumbersome, particularly when handling irregularly shaped or numerous food items. Additionally, existing choppers often lack means for stabilizing food during the chopping stroke, which can result in uneven chopping, food items shifting or escaping the chamber, and reduced overall chopping efficiency. There exists a need for a food chopper that allows for hands-free loading and provides reliable food stabilization while maintaining ease of cleaning and operation.

### Summary

The present invention addresses the aforementioned shortcomings by providing a manual food chopper comprising:

1. **A housing** defining a chopping chamber configured to receive food items, the housing including a base, side walls, and an open top for access to the chamber;

2. **A blade assembly** disposed within the chopping chamber, operably coupled to the pusher arm such that downward movement of the pusher arm drives the blade assembly through the food items;

3. **A pusher arm** pivotally connected to the housing, the pusher arm comprising:
   - A handle portion configured for gripping by a user;
   - A drive portion operably coupled to the blade assembly;
   - A self-retaining mechanism, which may include a spring-loaded detent, cam lock, over-center linkage, or friction hinge, configured to maintain the pusher arm in an open position absent user-applied closing force, and to release automatically upon application of a threshold downward force by the user;

4. **A retractable food stabilizer** disposed within or adjacent to the chopping chamber, the stabilizer comprising:
   - A stabilizing surface or plurality of prongs/tines configured to contact and restrain food items positioned within the chamber;
   - An actuation mechanism, which may include a slide button, lever, spring-biased plunger, or rotational cam, configured to move the stabilizer between an extended position and a retracted position;
   - Wherein the extended position engages food items to prevent lateral displacement during chopping, and the retracted position withdraws the stabilizer from the chopping chamber to permit unobstructed food loading, accommodate larger food items, or facilitate cleaning of the chamber.

### Advantages

The disclosed food chopper provides several advantages over the prior art, including but not limited to:

- **Hands-free loading**: The self-retaining pusher arm eliminates the need for a user to hold the arm open, freeing both hands for food preparation and loading.

- **Improved chopping consistency**: The retractable stabilizer secures food items in place, reducing shifting and resulting in more uniform chopping results.

- **Enhanced safety**: By securing food items and providing a controlled release mechanism for the pusher arm, the risk of user injury or food escaping the chamber is reduced.

- **Ease of cleaning**: The retractable nature of the stabilizer allows it to be withdrawn for simplified cleaning access to the chopping chamber.

- **Versatility**: The retractable stabilizer accommodates food items of varying sizes and shapes by selectively engaging or disengaging as needed.

### Brief Description of Alternative Embodiments

In certain embodiments, the self-retaining mechanism of the pusher arm may be implemented using a torsion spring combined with a mechanical stop, a ratcheting hinge, or a magnetic latch. In other embodiments, the retractable stabilizer may be integrated into the lid of the chopping chamber, the interior side wall, or the pusher arm itself, and may be actuated manually by the user or automatically in coordination with the movement of the pusher arm via a linked mechanical coupling. The stabilizer may further include a plurality of independently retractable segments to accommodate irregularly shaped food items.

### Brief Description of the Drawings *(placeholder for figures)*

- **FIG. 1**: Perspective view of the food chopper in the open/loading configuration, showing the pusher arm in its self-retained open position and the stabilizer in the retracted position.
- **FIG. 2**: Perspective view of the food chopper during the chopping stroke, showing the stabilizer in the extended position engaging a food item.
- **FIG. 3**: Cross-sectional side view illustrating the self-retaining detent mechanism of the pusher arm.
- **FIG. 4**: Cross-sectional side view illustrating the actuation mechanism of the retractable stabilizer.
- **FIG. 5**: Exploded view of the chopper assembly showing the housing, blade assembly, pusher arm, and stabilizer components.

---

*Note: This document is a drafted template for a patent application abstract and summary section. Actual filing would require consultation with a registered patent attorney or agent, along with detailed claims, complete drawings, and a full specification meeting USPTO or relevant jurisdictional requirements.*

# PATENT DISCLOSURE

## TITLE OF INVENTION
**Thrust-Type Food Slicer Having a Self-Stable Resting-Open Pusher Arm and Movable Fulcrum Pivot Mechanism**

---

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001] The present disclosure relates generally to manual food preparation devices, and more particularly to a thrust-type food slicer incorporating a pusher arm assembly that automatically returns to and maintains a stable, open resting position without operator intervention, in combination with a pivot mechanism having a fulcrum point that translates along a guide path during the cutting stroke to vary mechanical advantage and pusher trajectory.

---

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

[0002] Conventional manual thrust-type slicers typically employ a pusher arm pivotally fixed at a single, stationary point relative to a housing or carriage. Such arrangements present two persistent shortcomings. First, the pusher arm frequently lacks any inherent bias toward an open or raised position, requiring the operator to manually lift and hold the arm between cutting strokes, or relying on friction at the pivot, which degrades over time and permits the arm to sag or drift into the food-receiving zone unintentionally. Second, a fixed-fulcrum pivot imposes a constant mechanical advantage and a fixed arcuate trajectory upon the pusher pad throughout the stroke, which can cause the pad to disengage from optimal contact angle with the food product as the stroke progresses, resulting in uneven slice thickness, food slippage, or increased operator force requirements near the end of the stroke.

[0003] There exists a need for a thrust-type slicer pusher mechanism that (i) self-stabilizes in a fully open, ready-to-load position without auxiliary latches, springs requiring manual release, or operator effort, and (ii) provides a pivot point that itself translates during the stroke so as to modulate mechanical advantage and pad orientation dynamically, improving cut consistency and reducing operator fatigue.

---

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0004] Disclosed herein is a thrust-type food slicer comprising a base assembly, a blade assembly mounted to the base assembly and defining a cutting plane, a food carriage configured for reciprocating translation relative to the blade assembly, and a pusher arm assembly operatively coupled to the food carriage.

[0005] The pusher arm assembly includes a pusher arm having a proximal handle portion and a distal food-engaging portion, the pusher arm being pivotally coupled to a fulcrum bracket by a first pivot pin defining a pivot axis. In accordance with the disclosed embodiments, the pusher arm assembly is configured such that, absent an applied downward or forward thrust force, the pusher arm self-stabilizes in a fully open resting orientation by virtue of a deliberately offset center of mass relative to the pivot axis, an integrated biasing element, and/or a detent geometry formed at the fulcrum bracket—without requiring a manually-set latch, external clip, or continuous operator support.

[0006] The fulcrum bracket itself is not fixed relative to the carriage or base, but rather is mounted to a second pivot pin that is slidably or rotatably received within an elongated guide channel formed in the carriage frame, such that the effective fulcrum location translates along a defined path as the pusher arm is thrust through its cutting stroke. This movable-fulcrum arrangement varies the effective lever arm length and the instantaneous trajectory of the food-engaging portion during the stroke, thereby maintaining a more consistent contact angle and pressure profile against the food product as it is advanced past the blade assembly, and reducing peak operator force typically required near stroke termination in fixed-fulcrum designs.

[0007] A return-biasing element, such as a coil, torsion, or leaf spring, is optionally coupled between the fulcrum bracket and the carriage frame to urge the fulcrum pin back to its initial position within the guide channel upon release of thrust force, cooperatively restoring the pusher arm to its self-stable open position.

---

## BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS

[0008] FIG. 1 illustrates a perspective view of the thrust-type food slicer in the resting-open configuration.

[0009] FIG. 2 illustrates a side elevational, partially cross-sectioned view of the pusher arm assembly showing the fulcrum bracket, first pivot pin, and guide channel.

[0010] FIG. 3 illustrates the pusher arm assembly at an intermediate position during a cutting stroke, depicting translation of the fulcrum pin within the guide channel.

[0011] FIG. 4 illustrates the pusher arm assembly at full stroke extension, proximate the blade assembly.

[0012] FIG. 5 illustrates an alternative embodiment employing a detent-based self-stabilization feature in place of, or in addition to, center-of-mass offset.

---

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS

### General Arrangement

[0013] Referring to FIG. 1, the food slicer 10 comprises a base 12 supporting a blade assembly 20 having a cutting edge 22 disposed along a fixed cutting plane. A food carriage 30 is slidably mounted upon rails or tracks 32 formed in or affixed to base 12, permitting reciprocating translation of carriage 30 toward and away from blade assembly 20. Carriage 30 defines a food-receiving surface 34 configured to receive a food product to be sliced.

### Pusher Arm Assembly

[0014] A pusher arm assembly 40 is operatively mounted to carriage 30. Pusher arm assembly 40 comprises a pusher arm 42 having a proximal handle portion 42a configured for manual engagement, and a distal food-engaging portion 42b, such as a pusher pad or food guard, configured to contact an upper or rearward surface of the food product.

[0015] Pusher arm 42 is pivotally coupled at an intermediate location to a fulcrum bracket 50 via a first pivot pin 44 defining a first pivot axis A1. Fulcrum bracket 50 is, in turn, mounted to carriage 30 via a second pivot/slide pin 52 (the "fulcrum pin") received within an elongated guide channel 60 formed in a side wall or bracket structure of carriage 30.

### Self-Stable Resting-Open Configuration

[0016] In accordance with a first embodiment, self-stabilization of pusher arm 42 in the open resting position is achieved through deliberate placement of the center of mass CM of pusher arm 42 rearward of pivot axis A1, relative to the direction of the cutting stroke. As a result, in the absence of an applied thrust force, gravitational torque about pivot axis A1 continuously urges pusher arm 42 rotationally upward and rearward into a mechanical stop 46 formed on fulcrum bracket 50, defining a repeatable, stable open position without requiring a separate latch or the operator's continued manual support.

[0017] In accordance with an alternative or supplementary embodiment (FIG. 5), a detent feature 48, such as a spring-loaded ball detent or a compliant geometric lobe, is formed at or near pivot pin 44, cooperating with a complementary recess formed in fulcrum bracket 50 such that pusher arm 42 is releasably retained in the open position with a defined minimum threshold force, while still permitting free rotation into the cutting stroke upon application of ordinary thrust force by the operator.

[0018] It will be appreciated that the self-stabilizing feature may be implemented through center-of-mass offset alone, detent geometry alone, a calibrated torsion spring disposed about pivot pin 44 alone, or any combination thereof, without departing from the scope of the present disclosure.

### Movable Fulcrum Pivot Mechanism

[0019] Distinct from the pivotal connection of pusher arm 42 to fulcrum bracket 50, the fulcrum bracket 50 itself is coupled to carriage 30 through fulcrum pin 52, which is slidably and/or rotatably captured within guide channel 60. Guide channel 60 may be linear, arcuate,

# Invention Summary: Kitchen Food Processing Apparatus with Self-Resting Pivoting Arm and Retractable Stabilizer

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates generally to manual kitchen food preparation tools, and more particularly to a food slicing/processing apparatus comprising a blade assembly, a food pusher mechanism, a pivoting support arm configured to automatically rest in an open position, and a retractable stabilizer bar for enhanced operational stability.

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention provides a kitchen tool apparatus comprising, in combination:

**(a) A blade assembly**, comprising one or more cutting blades fixedly or removably disposed within a housing, said blade assembly configured to receive and process food items therethrough;

**(b) A food pusher member**, slidably engaged with the housing and configured to advance food items into operative contact with the blade assembly, said pusher member comprising a gripping surface and a food-engaging face substantially complementary to a receiving channel of the housing;

**(c) A pivoting arm**, operatively coupled to the housing via a hinge mechanism, said pivoting arm being movable between a closed position and an open position, and further comprising a biasing element configured to automatically urge and maintain said pivoting arm in the open position absent an external closing force, thereby enabling hands-free operation and access to the blade assembly; and

**(d) A retractable stabilizer bar**, slidably or telescopically disposed within a base portion of the housing, said stabilizer bar being selectively extendable from a retracted position substantially flush with or contained within said base portion to an extended position projecting outwardly therefrom, said extended position configured to engage a support surface and increase a footprint of the apparatus so as to resist tipping or lateral movement during operation, and said stabilizer bar being further configured to return to the retracted position for compact storage.

## Exemplary Claim Language

**Claim 1.** A kitchen food processing apparatus comprising:
a housing defining a food-receiving channel;
a blade assembly disposed within the housing;
a food pusher slidably received within the food-receiving channel and configured to urge food items against the blade assembly;
a pivoting arm hingedly connected to the housing, the pivoting arm including a biasing means configured to automatically maintain the pivoting arm in an open position when unengaged; and
a stabilizer bar movably coupled to the housing, the stabilizer bar being selectively deployable between a retracted position and an extended position, wherein in the extended position the stabilizer bar increases lateral stability of the apparatus relative to a supporting surface.

**Claim 2.** The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the biasing means comprises a spring, torsion element, or gravity-actuated detent configured to bias the pivoting arm toward the open position.

**Claim 3.** The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the stabilizer bar is spring-loaded and configured to automatically retract into the housing upon release of a locking mechanism.

**Claim 4.** The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the food pusher further comprises a locking feature configured to releasably secure the food pusher in a raised position relative to the housing.

# UNITED STATES PATENT APPLICATION

## MECHANICAL FOOD CUTTER WITH SELF-STABILIZING PUSHER ARM AND SYNCHRONIZED RETRACTABLE FOOD STABILIZER

---

### FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates generally to manually or mechanically actuated food preparation devices, and more particularly to a mechanical food cutter comprising a chassis, a pivoting link assembly, a self-stabilizing pusher arm, and a retractable food stabilizer that is synchronized with the motion of the pusher arm to secure food items during a cutting operation.

---

### BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Manual food cutting devices are commonly used to slice, dice, or portion food items such as fruits, vegetables, and soft solids. Conventional devices typically rely on a simple lever-actuated blade assembly that requires the user to manually hold the food item in place during the cutting stroke. This presents several disadvantages, including inconsistent cutting results due to food shifting during the cutting stroke, risk of injury to the user's fingers, and lack of mechanical synchronization between the food-holding mechanism and the cutting mechanism.

There exists a need in the art for a food cutting apparatus that automatically stabilizes the food item during the cutting stroke without requiring separate manual manipulation by the user, while also providing a self-stabilizing pusher arm that maintains consistent alignment and pressure throughout the cutting motion.

---

### SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The present invention addresses the foregoing needs by providing a mechanical food cutter comprising:

(a) a chassis defining a support structure and a food-receiving region;

(b) a pivoting link operatively coupled to the chassis and configured to translate an input actuation force into a controlled displacement;

(c) a self-stabilizing pusher arm coupled to the pivoting link, the pusher arm being configured to maintain a substantially constant orientation relative to the food-receiving region throughout its range of motion, thereby applying consistent downward or lateral force to a food item during the cutting operation; and

(d) a retractable food stabilizer mechanically synchronized with the pusher arm via the pivoting link, the food stabilizer being configured to extend into engagement with the food item prior to or concurrent with the initiation of the cutting stroke, and to retract automatically upon completion of the stroke, thereby permitting removal of cut food portions without manual intervention.

The synchronization between the pusher arm and the retractable food stabilizer is achieved through a shared mechanical linkage, cam surface, or biasing member, such that a single actuation input produces coordinated, sequential motion of both the pusher arm and the stabilizer.

---

### BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS

**FIG. 1** is a perspective view of the mechanical food cutter in a fully retracted, pre-actuation state.

**FIG. 2** is a perspective view of the mechanical food cutter in a fully actuated, cutting state, illustrating the extended position of the pusher arm and the engaged position of the food stabilizer.

**FIG. 3** is a side elevational cross-sectional view illustrating the pivoting link assembly and its mechanical connection to both the pusher arm and the retractable food stabilizer.

**FIG. 4** is a detail view of the self-stabilizing pivot joint of the pusher arm.

**FIG. 5** is a schematic diagram illustrating the synchronized motion path of the pusher arm and food stabilizer over a single actuation cycle.

---

### DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS

Referring now to the drawings, wherein like reference numerals refer to like elements throughout the several views, there is shown in **FIG. 1** a mechanical food cutter, generally designated **10**, comprising a chassis **12**, a pivoting link **20**, a self-stabilizing pusher arm **30**, and a retractable food stabilizer **40**.

#### The Chassis

The chassis **12** comprises a rigid frame constructed of metal, reinforced polymer, or a combination thereof, and defines a base **14**, a pair of upstanding side walls **16***a*, **16***b*, and a food-receiving region **18** disposed between the side walls **16***a*, **16***b*. The chassis **12** further defines a blade-mounting aperture **19** disposed beneath the food-receiving region **18**, configured to receive a cutting blade or blade array (not shown) in a fixed or removable manner. The chassis **12** provides structural support for all moving components of the device and may further include mounting features **13** for securing the device to a countertop or supplemental base.

#### The Pivoting Link

The pivoting link **20** is rotatably mounted to the chassis **12** at a first pivot axis **22**, and comprises an elongated rigid member having a proximal end **24** coupled to an actuation input, such as a handle **26**, and a distal end **28** operatively coupled to the pusher arm **30**. Rotation of the pivoting link **20** about the first pivot axis **22**, in response to a user-applied or motor-applied actuation force at the handle **26**, produces a corresponding arcuate or translational displacement at the distal end **28**.

In certain embodiments, the pivoting link **20** further comprises a secondary linkage arm **21** extending from an intermediate portion thereof, the secondary linkage arm **21** being operatively coupled to the retractable food stabilizer **40**, as described in greater detail below, such that a single rotational input at the pivoting link **20** produces coordinated motion at both the pusher arm **30** and the food stabilizer **40**.

#### The Self-Stabilizing Pusher Arm

The pusher arm **30** is coupled to the distal end **28** of the pivoting link **20** via a self-stabilizing pivot joint **32**. The self-stabilizing pivot joint **32** comprises a secondary pivot axis **34** and a biasing element **36**, such as a torsion spring, disposed to bias the pusher arm **30** toward a substantially normal orientation relative to the food-receiving region **18** regardless of the angular position of the pivoting link **20**.

This configuration allows the pusher arm **30** to maintain a consistent contact angle and pressure distribution against the food item throughout the cutting stroke, notwithstanding the arcuate motion imparted by the pivoting link **20**. The self-stabilizing pivot joint **32** may further include a guide slot **38** and a corresponding guide pin **39** fixed to the chassis **12**, wherein the guide pin **39** rides within the guide slot **38** to constrain the orientation of the pusher arm **30** as it translates through its range of motion, further preventing rotational drift or misalignment of the pusher arm **30** relative to the food item during the cutting stroke.

The pusher arm **30** further comprises a contact face **35** dimensioned to engage an upper surface of a food item positioned within the food-receiving region **18**, the contact face **35** optionally comprising a compliant or textured material to enhance grip and distribute contact pressure evenly across the food item.

#### The Retractable Food Stabilizer

The retractable food stabilizer **40** is slidably mounted to the chassis **12** within a stabilizer channel **42** disposed adjacent to the food-receiving region **18**. The food stabilizer **40** comprises an engagement tine or plate **44** configured to extend into contact with a lateral or upper surface of the food item, and a return biasing member **46**, such as a compression spring, configured to urge the food stabilizer **40** toward a retracted position absent an opposing actuation force.

The food stabilizer **40** is mechanically coupled to the secondary linkage arm **21** of the pivoting link **20** via a coupling rod **48** or, alternatively, via a cam-follower arrangement comprising a cam surface **50** disposed on the pivoting link **20** and a follower element **52** disposed on the food stabilizer **40**. As the pivoting link **20** rotates in response to actuation, the cam surface **50** or coupling rod **48** drives the food stabilizer **40** from a retracted position to an extended, food-engaging position in advance of, or concurrently with, the descent of the pusher arm **30**.

This synchronization ensures that the food item is engaged and immobilized by the food stabilizer **40** prior to the application of cutting force by the pusher arm **30**, thereby preventing shifting, rolling, or slippage of the food item during the cutting stroke. Upon reversal of the actuation force and return of the pivoting link **20** to its initial position, the return biasing member **46** automatically retracts the food stabilizer **40**, permitting removal of the cut food portions from the food-receiving region **18**.

#### Operation

In operation, a user applies an actuation force to the handle **26**, causing the pivoting link **20** to rotate about the first pivot axis **22**. This rotation produces two substantially concurrent effects: (1) the secondary linkage arm **21** or cam surface **50** drives the retractable food stabilizer **40** from its retracted position into engagement with the food item positioned in the food-receiving region **18**; and (2) the distal end **28** of the pivoting link **20** drives the self-stabilizing pusher arm **30** downward into contact with the food item, wherein the self-stabilizing pivot joint **32** maintains the contact face **35** in a substantially constant orientation throughout the stroke.

Continued actuation drives the pusher arm **30** through the food item and into or through the blade-mounting aperture **19**, effecting a cutting operation. Upon release of the actuation force, the biasing element **36** and return biasing member **46** cooperate to return the pusher arm **30** and food stabilizer **40**, respectively, to their initial retracted positions, in preparation for a subsequent cutting cycle.

# Summary of Invention

The present invention relates to a manual food dicing apparatus configured to safely and efficiently cut vegetables, fruits, and other food products into uniform pieces. More particularly, the invention provides a dicer having an open-resting pusher arm mechanism and a retractable stabilizing element that cooperate to hold food securely in place during the cutting operation while enhancing user safety and ease of use.

In one aspect, the invention comprises a base having a cutting grid disposed thereon or therein, the cutting grid comprising a plurality of intersecting blades arranged to divide food product into uniform cubes, strips, or other predetermined shapes upon application of downward force. The base further includes a receptacle or chamber positioned beneath the cutting grid for collecting the diced food product after it passes through the blades.

A pusher arm is pivotally coupled to the base and is movable between a raised, open-resting position and a lowered, cutting position. In the open-resting position, the pusher arm remains stably suspended above the cutting grid without requiring the user to manually hold or support it, thereby freeing the user's hands to position the food product on the cutting grid or to operate the retractable stabilizing element. This open-resting configuration is achieved through a biasing mechanism, detent, counterweight, or friction-hinge arrangement that maintains the pusher arm in the raised position until an intentional downward force is applied by the user, at which point the pusher arm pivots downward to drive the food product through the cutting grid.

The retractable stabilizing element is disposed on or adjacent to the base and is movable between an extended position, in which it engages and holds the food product in a fixed orientation atop the cutting grid, and a retracted position, in which it is withdrawn to allow unobstructed placement and removal of food product and to permit unimpeded operation of the pusher arm during the cutting stroke. The stabilizing element may comprise a spring-loaded plate, clamp, or gripping member that can be manually or automatically deployed to secure food items of varying sizes and shapes, thereby preventing unwanted shifting, rolling, or slippage during the dicing operation.

In operation, a user places a food item on the cutting grid, engages the retractable stabilizing element to secure the food item in position, and then applies downward force to the pusher arm—which, owing to its open-resting configuration, requires no preliminary manual positioning—to drive the food item through the cutting grid and produce uniformly diced pieces. Following the cutting stroke, the stabilizing element may be retracted to permit removal of any remaining food product or insertion of a new item, and the pusher arm returns to its open-resting position in preparation for a subsequent cutting cycle.

The combination of the open-resting pusher arm mechanism and the retractable stabilizing element provides several advantages over conventional manual dicing devices, including improved user safety by reducing the risk of hand injury during food positioning, enhanced cutting accuracy and consistency due to reduced food movement during the cutting stroke, and increased operational efficiency by eliminating the need for the user to manually hold the pusher arm between cutting cycles. Various embodiments of the invention may further include interchangeable cutting grids of differing blade spacing or configuration, adjustable stabilizing elements accommodating food items of different sizes, and locking mechanisms for securing the pusher arm in either the open-resting or cutting position as desired.

These and other features, aspects, and advantages of the present invention will become apparent from the following detailed description, appended claims, and accompanying drawings.
